source.title: From Refusal Geometry to Safety Geometry: Harmfulness--Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Wen-Hao Lan; Shan Li; Xin Lai; Mei-Qi Wu; Jun-Bin Yang; Hai-Hua Shen; Yi-Jun Yang

page_placements.theme: Harm recognition can survive refusal failure

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates GCG jailbreak attack success on checkpoints across fine-tuning trajectories, bearing on whether attacks can overcome safety behavior. Its H/R coupling measurements are a different method and construct from the claim’s per-token KL and parameter-localization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures H/R carrier overlap, not per-token KL across aligned and base models; it does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes. It reports GCG fixed-source attack success and selected activation-carrier interventions. The training data contents and example counts are not stated, so the SFT and R2D2 trajectories do not establish the harmful-example or benign-instruction-data conditions in V1 or V2. Dense all-anchor correlations and sparse-transfer predictor comparisons do not report attack success rates by transfer condition in the main text; they are not extracted as attack-rate rows.
record.test_reason: The paper's question is harmfulness–refusal (H/R) coupling across Mistral-7B-v0.1 SFT and R2D2 trajectories. Fixed-source HarmBench GCG ASR serves only as a behaviour readout next to the coupling index. No unattacked harmful-request compliance rate is reported for any checkpoint, so suffix-driven bypass (V4) cannot be separated from the model simply complying. R2D2 is adversarial training against GCG, not a test of whether suffixes defeat refusal. Mistral-7B-v0.1 is a base model, so the SFT run is not fine-tuning of a safety-aligned model, and the data contents are unstated; V1 and V2 are not tested. There is no per-token KL analysis, no weight or rank localization, and no first-token deepening. The activation-carrier ablations and steering are a related construct, not V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. R2D2 passes through distinct H/R coupling regimes with different robustness, over-refusal and utility profiles. SFT shows that low coupling is not a safety score. The authors frame H/R coupling as a fixed-protocol training diagnostic, not proof of independent pathways or a deployment predictor.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies matched Mistral SFT and R2D2 training trajectories and H/R activation-carrier coupling; it does not report fine-tuning on a stated few-to-hundreds-example harmful or benign dataset. It also evaluates GCG/AutoDAN attacks rather than compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by training regime and checkpoint: R2D2 attack success is zero early and increases at later anchors, while SFT remains high-ASR across its five anchors. The authors also report that intervention effects depend on carrier mode and matched controls.

fits_no_version.finding: Under continued R2D2 adversarial training, GCG ASR rises from 0 to 0.25 by step 500. Over the same steps XSTest refusal falls from 1.0 to 0.228 and benign helpfulness recovers from 0 to 1.12, while H/R coupling drops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial-training robustness to GCG erodes later in training as over-refusal relaxes and utility returns.

fits_no_version.finding: H/R coupling index trajectories: a large drop under R2D2, small change under SFT, and low coupling coexisting with high ASR in SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: H/R representational coupling tracks training regime but is not a safety score.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the refusal carrier reopens HarmBench ASR much more than ablating the harmfulness carrier. In Llama, R-only ablation gives 0.6825 against a 0.1675 baseline, versus 0.14 for H-only. Mistral sweep effects are small relative to matched controls, and the reopened outputs are often empty or nonsensical.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-side activation carriers act as a causal bottleneck for refusal, separate from harmfulness recognition.

record.code_released: The paper says the artifact package will be deposited in a public archival repository upon acceptance; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The main trajectory uses one Mistral backbone and one completed training run per regime. The authors describe dense correlations and sparse transfer as descriptive and fixed-protocol, note that sparse-transfer comparisons are small-n and partly collinear with behavior predictors, and state that controls are not matched to raw activation-delta norms. The benign utility set has 60 prompts. The paper does not report uncertainty for the five-anchor Table 2 ASR values.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: Table 3 dense all-anchor Spearman associations (reported as descriptive correlations, not attack-rate results); Table 5 sparse-transfer predictor correlations (not per-condition transfer ASR values); and the 43-row intervention-level follow-up's aggregate means because it does not give separate subject-by-condition outcomes. The full causal-sweep matrix is not enumerated in the main text; Table 4's eight representative rows are extracted. The paper also reports StrongREJECT, XSTest refusal, and benign-helpfulness trajectory values, but these do not measure the behaviors named by V1–V4.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of a safety-aligned model on a counted set of harmful examples.
No benign-data fine-tuning of an aligned model; the SFT data are unstated and start from a base model.
No per-token KL by response position.
No prefilling or decoding attacks. GCG and AutoDAN ASR is reported without a no-attack baseline.
No weight or rank localization; the interventions are on activation carriers only.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 supports and limits_scope labels are removed. The GCG ASR values carry no unattacked baseline. The SFT trajectory starts from base Mistral-7B-v0.1, not from a safety-aligned model. R2D2 is a GCG-targeted defence, so its ASR values do not speak to whether suffixes bypass shallow alignment. One backbone and one run per regime were used. The study cites Qi et al. (one of the original sources) only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not state that the fine-tuning used a few to a few hundred harmful examples or report harmful-example counts.
The SFT data are not described as ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data; the paper does not test that data condition.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models, or analysis of KL by response position.
Tests GCG and AutoDAN attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes; sparse-transfer results are reported as predictor correlations rather than per-condition transfer ASR values.
No weight or rank localization experiment.
Does not test whether data or a training objective produces first-token shallowness.
Does not train safety to spread beyond the first tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: Uses GCG and AutoDAN attacks to assess coupling and robustness; does not directly test opening bypass, parameter localization, or the other specified versions.

tranche.reason: Uses jailbreak attacks as behavioral readouts for an H/R-coupling diagnostic. The reported activation interventions and training trajectories do not isolate an effect named by the catalog's claim versions.

source_check.notes: Table 4 Δcontrol values are contrasts, not uncertainty estimates. The supplied text is arXiv:2606.16349v3, titled Tracking Harmfulness–Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning; the pack gives a different title.

reader_labels.reason: Fixed-source GCG ASR is 0.5050–0.6400 at the five SFT anchors, showing attack success in this setting (T2-SFT-ref-ASR, T2-SFT-50-ASR, T2-SFT-100-ASR, T2-SFT-250-ASR, T2-SFT-500-ASR).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Attack success is zero at reference, step 50, and step 100, then only 0.0350 and 0.2500 at steps 250 and 500; the attack effect is trajectory-dependent and partial (T2-R2D2-ref-ASR, T2-R2D2-50-ASR, T2-R2D2-100-ASR, T2-R2D2-250-ASR, T2-R2D2-500-ASR).
